episodes.193187: The monsoon high shifted east of New Mexico on August 12th resulting in a traditional monsoon setup over the state. Storms developed over the Sacramento Mountains midday August 12th producing heavy rainfall over the South Fork and Salt Fire burn scars. This resulted in flash flooding and higher flows in the Upper Canyon neighborhood and the closure of bridges in the area. Storms dissipated during the evening hours.
episodes.193237: A thunderstorm moving offshore produced gusty winds along the Volusia County coastline.
episodes.193505: Severe thunderstorms developed across Goshen and Laramie Counties the afternoon of 12 August.
episodes.193995: Slow moving thunderstorms produced flash flooding with up to four inches of rainfall reported in Brush and north of Punkin Center. In addition to the heavy rainfall, hail up to two inches in diameter and 68 mph winds were reported.
episodes.194024: Southwest steering flow pushed the stronger west coast sea breeze toward the Atlantic coast in the evening where sea breeze and boundary mergers produced stronger storms with gusty winds.
episodes.194122: A weak cold front noted across the Coastal Plain slowly tracked east throughout the day on August 12th, eventually pushing off the Coast during the evening hours bringing isolated to widely scattered showers and thunderstorms to the coast and offshore waters of Eastern North Carolina. A few of these storms brought damaging wind gusts to portions of the Pamlico Sound and coastal waters near the Core Banks.
episodes.194250: A southwesterly flow aloft combined with ample surface heating to result in deep inverted-V soundings. Thunderstorms that formed along the Rocky Mountain Front moved eastward through the afternoon and early evening, resulting in a few strong wind gusts. This episode will also contain a gust from the Dillon area on the 15th from strong outflow. Deep inverted-V soundings supported this stronger gust.
episodes.194326: A few isolated thunderstorms produced some severe wind gusts.
episodes.194429: A strong low-level jet emerged across central into northern Oklahoma during the early morning of the 12th. This feature promoted scattered thunderstorm development across these areas, with one thunderstorm producing a severe-caliber wind gust event.
episodes.195092: A slow moving thunderstorm brought heavy rain and small hail to Opal. The rain and hail overwhelmed the street sewers and resulted in flooding of 5 houses and a few streets.
episodes.195105: Strong thunderstorm activity developed over the San Diego Mountains during the afternoon hours on the 11th, likely instigated by large-scale forcing for ascent from an upper-level low located to the south. Outflows from the initial thunderstorm complex over the San Diego mountains helped to initialize new activity across western Imperial County. With PWAT values of around 2.0 inches, conditions were favorable for heavy rainfall producing thunderstorms.
episodes.195117: In the early afternoon of the 11th, a single thunderstorm formed in northeastern Colorado and moved southeast into Kansas. In northwest Kansas, winds up to an estimated 80 MPH flipped an irrigation pivot and caused tree damage.  Golf ball size hail was also reported.
episodes.195322: Slow moving thunderstorms produced isolated areas of flash flooding.
episodes.195424: Monsoon moisture and hot temperatures fueled scattered thunderstorms over northwest Arizona. A few storms produced severe weather and flash flooding.
episodes.195499: Deep monsoonal moisture remained in place with convection ongoing during the morning hours. This led to a later start to convection on the afternoon of August 11th but precipitable water values climbed to over an inch as deep monsoonal moisture continued to increase from the south, combined with a shortwave trough and sufficient lift from an upper level jet helped provide support for stronger storms towards the late afternoon and evening that led to 1 to 2 inch per hour rainfall rates on top of already saturated soils leading to significant debris flows and flash flooding, especially across southwest Colorado.
episodes.195522: Storms developed over the Sandhills and Coastal Plain along a stalled frontal zone. Most of the storms were below severe limits, but a few produced flash flooding and downed power lines in Nash and Cumberland Counties.
episodes.195524: Storms developed early in the morning of the 12th of August over the southern Piedmont, Sandhills, and southern Coastal Plain in association with a surface low tracking along a stalled frontal boundary. Storms produced nearly 2 inch hail over Moore County, as well as downed trees and power lines in Cumberland County.
episodes.195877: Thunderstorms developed along a stationary front, situated in the western Nebraska Panhandle during the afternoon of August 11th. As this activity drifted east, storms became severe. Hail up to the size of ping pong balls and thunderstorm wind gusts up to 70 MPH were reported with the strongest storms.
episodes.195888: A late evening severe thunderstorm pushed through Graham County south of Safford resulting in wind gusts over 70 mph.
episodes.195949: Deep moisture and a stalled frontal boundary left the area very susceptible to flash flooding from isolated, slow moving storms.
episodes.196060: Monsoonal showers and thunderstorms brought gusty winds and flash flooding to much of Utah.
episodes.196061: An upper level shortwave trough destabilized atmosphere environment that led to numerous thunderstorms and heavy rain. Several thunderstorms occurred over the crest of the Cascades near Easy and Rainy Passes that caused multiple flash floods and debris flows off the mountain ridge along and northeast of State Route 20 that buried the highway in multiple locations.
episodes.196072: Monsoonal showers and thunderstorms brought flash flooding and gusty winds to Utah.
episodes.196073: With a mid-level monsoonal moisture plume already in place, and a passing shortwave trough in the upper levels, a few strong to severe storms developed over portions of the plains from the 12th thru 13th of August, and also resulted in some heavy amounts of rain over El Paso County. A wet microburst from a thunderstorm also produced wind damage around the city of Pueblo due to brief gusty winds being greater than hurricane force.
episodes.196083: Ample monoon moisture and slow moving thunderstorms brought lightning, heavy rain, and flash flooding to a few locations across northern Arizona.
episodes.196162: Debris flow occurred on Davelaar Dr near Looney Creek as a result of heavy rain on the Cedar Creek burn scar.
episodes.196258: A monsoon surge occurred on Sunday August 11, 2024. Numerous strong to severe thunderstorms erupted across the San Diego mountains and into the Riverside County mountains. Thunderstorms produced hail, wind gusts and rainfall rates of 1 inch in 60 minutes.

Video showing flash flooding in multiple spots along Split Mountain Rd, with most significant flooding at the Fish Creek Wash crossing. The road was washed out at this point and floodwaters were reportedly as deep as 4-6 feet based on sediment flow and depth of the wash. No injuries were reported.

Heavy rain from a couple of thunderstorms fell over the mountain ridge, above the recent Easy Fire burn scar, with the main period of heavy rain lasting about one hour and 45 minutes starting 1800PST. Flash floods and debris flows came out of several drainages along and northeast of State Route 20 between mile post 151 and 152.5, burying the highway. The debris flows initiated above the burn scar and little of the flood debris was from the burn scar itself. It took two weeks to clean up and fix the highway to make it passable. |Rain rates from a nearby rain gage along the highway were up to 0.29 inches in 15 minutes, 0.53 inches in 30 minutes, 0.96 inches in 1 hour, and a two hour storm total of 1.28 inches. No injuries or fatalities occurred.
SR-98 closed between Imperial Highway and Brockman Road due to flooding with several vehicles hydroplaning on the road. No damages nor injuries were reported.

Very heavy rain in the mountains above Littlefield flowed down into the community, leaving the Farm/Fleet Rd underpass under I-15 flooded with approximately 10 feet of water. Other roads in the area were also flooded, including the northbound lanes of I-15 near mile marker 9.

Steady heavy rains during the evening of August 11th resulted in multiple mudslides and flooding overnight in east Telluride, Bridal Veil Falls Area and Tomboy Road. This resulted in closures of several nearby passes including from the East Spur at the Town of Telluride entrance east to Black Bear, Black Bear Pass itself, Tomboy Road and Imogene Pass. Time of event was based on radar estimate.

Heavy rain from thunderstorms in Ouray caused town flooding as well as the flooding of several creeks including Oak, Cascade and Skyrocket Creek. These creeks filled with debris, rock and silt, resulting in trail closures and large boulders/rock slides and mudslides on Highway 550 at mile marker 94, 94.5 and 94.6 specifically but generally between mile markers 94 and 95 approximately 2 miles north-northwest of Ouray.  Storm total rainfall ranged from 1.5 to 1.7 inches in Ouray. Daily spot forecasts were requested by emergency management for both Ridgway and Ouray for extensive cleanup efforts for several days following the debris flows.
